summary: Built on the opus skeleton, which was the only variant both reviewers rated sound-with-repairs and the only one whose parity story survives the fact that governs this initiative: apps/server/src/main.ts is imported by ZERO tests, so `pnpm gates` cannot fail for any main.ts wiring bug, and four of the eight findings live inside it. Sonnet's skeleton is discarded — its S2 relocated ~800 lines of 0%-coverage wiring in one commit on evidence that cannot fail (fable rated it FATAL, opus major), and its S4 unilaterally wired stop() into a fault counter, turning a throwing effect into a dead rig with no restart path 42ms into the fault; both reviewers killed it. Fable's subtraction-first instincts are grafted where they beat opus (the pure clientErrorMessage in the already-tested ws-protocol.ts rather than inline in a connection handler; the refusal of speculative knobs; sequencing economy), but its central weakness — four main.ts-wiring steps verified by grep, gates, and a citation of a boot.test.ts that does not exist — is exactly what the opus S0 instrument answers. The shape is therefore: build the boot-parity instrument FIRST, then strangler-drain main.ts one leaf at a time, every extraction a verbatim move in its own commit with the behaviour change that motivated it landing in a SEPARATE later commit against the now-testable module. Eight landed attacks forced changes visible in the steps: S0 now ships an explicit normalisation allow-list plus a NEGATIVE CONTROL (an injected change that must diff, otherwise the oracle is unproven); S1's false premise is repaired to the genuinely unpinned req.on('error') branch plus a boundary cap test; S3 darkens WITHOUT closing the transport and bounds process exit on the datagram drain, because dgram send is async and exit(1) is synchronous; S10 discriminates IO faults from corruption before renaming a drummer's project aside and recovers project+libraries from the SAME bundle; the slow-peer strike clock is decoupled from the 100 Hz broadcast cadence onto the 15s keepalive sweep and the skip is confined to the high-rate streams; the connection cap keeps a constant default with a single LEDRUMS_MAX_CLIENTS override; the keepalive lives in its own ws-keepalive.ts rather than in client-registry.ts, whose CloseableSocket contract is deliberately close()-only; and the ['S16','S18'] boot.ts wave collision is serialised. Two synthesis-owned questions are settled here: the two HTTP body caps stay per-route (2048 / 4096) because fable's unification is mechanically falsified by host-event.test.ts:205, and packages/core is never touched — the render-loop boundary sits at the VoiceEngineHost, since a quarantine set inside core is the hidden global state AGENTS.md forbids in a deterministic render loop.

design.title: Boot-parity smoke harness with an explicit normalisation contract and a negative control
design.intent: main.ts has no seam and no test, so nothing downstream can claim parity — every later main.ts commit needs an oracle that a green suite cannot provide. Build the instrument first: a harness that boots the real process in BOTH engine modes and reduces its observable startup behaviour to a stable digest. REPAIRED against the landed attack that S0's normalisation was unspecified and therefore gameable (the cheapest path to an empty diff is to normalise away exactly the fields that would have detected a regression): the step now ships a written allow-list of retained keys, a fixed redaction list, and a negative control proving the digest can still fail.
design.verification: Three gates, all required before any later step may cite the harness. (1) STABILITY: `node scripts/server-smoke.mjs --engine voice --out /tmp/a.json` twice, `diff /tmp/a.json /tmp/b.json` EMPTY; repeat with `--engine legacy`. (2) NORMALISATION CONTRACT: the harness header and artifacts/smoke-normalisation.md state, as an allow-list, exactly which keys are RETAINED in the digest (stdout banner lines with volatile substrings masked; the first `state` message's project/model/effects/output/showLibrary/songLibrary/tunnel/osc shapes; the first 3 `stats` frames' key sets; the ordered list of monitor events by {type,source,destination,label}) and, as a redaction list, exactly what is stripped (Date.now-derived ids incl. snapshot stems `${Date.now()}-boot` from snapshot-store.ts:110, client ids `c${n}` from client-registry.ts:49, ports, hostnames, randomUUIDs, mktemp absolute paths, host token, PIN, time/createdAt/latencyMs/fps/timeMs/beat/uptimeMs). Anything not on the allow-list is not in the digest; anything on it is never redacted. (3) NEGATIVE CONTROL: with the harness trusted, apply two scratch mutations to main.ts one at a time — (a) delete one monitor emit, (b) swap the presence-then-state ordering at main.ts:492-500 — and confirm EACH produces a non-empty digest diff; revert both. A mutation that does not diff means the digest is blind where it matters and S0 is not done.
design.reverses: Delete scripts/server-smoke.mjs, the normalisation note and the two baseline digests. Nothing in apps/ or packages/ is touched, so this step cannot regress the product.

design.title: Characterization test for native-MIDI's genuinely unpinned guard
design.intent: Before duplicated-code-0006's extraction moves the trusted-POST scaffolding, pin the guards that are about to move. REPAIRED against the landed attack that the original premise was factually false: native-midi.test.ts:145 ALREADY pins the 4KB cap (it sends 'x'.repeat(5000)). What is genuinely unpinned is the `req.on('error')` -> 400 branch, which has no case in that file. The cap test that does exist cannot detect a cap VALUE change (5000 is destroyed at both 2048 and 4096), so a boundary case is added alongside — that is the test that fails when the constant moves through the extraction.
design.verification: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec vitest run src/http/native-midi.test.ts` — two new cases green against UNMODIFIED native-midi.ts: (1) emitting 'error' on the fake request before 'end' yields status 400 body 'bad request' (the fake at native-midi.test.ts:50 already exposes `handlers.error`); (2) a BOUNDARY pair — a body of 'x'.repeat(4096) is accepted and reaches the decoder, a body of 'x'.repeat(4097) is destroyed with 'native MIDI payload too large'. Falsification check: temporarily set the cap to 2048 and confirm the boundary case FAILS (the pre-existing 5000-byte case does not, which is why it is insufficient); restore.
design.reverses: Revert the test file. Added coverage only; no source change.

design.title: Per-frame exception boundary in VoiceEngineHost.loop()
design.intent: resilience-hole-0001: `scheduleNext()` calls `loop()` in a bare setTimeout (voice-engine-host.ts:455-460) and nothing between it and gen.render() catches, so one throw in an authored effect kills the process and freezes the rig lit. Contain the fault at the HOST boundary — the outermost place that is still ours and still testable — not inside packages/core, where a quarantine counter would be the hidden global state AGENTS.md forbids in a deterministic render loop. The step buys survival of the loop and nothing more: it deliberately does NOT attempt per-effect quarantine, and it deliberately does NOT call stop() on a fault counter (sonnet's variant did; both reviewers killed it — stop() clears the timer, blackouts AND closes the transport with no restart path anywhere, so at 120fps a deterministically-throwing effect kills the whole rig in ~42ms and it stays dead until relaunch).
design.verification: New cases in voice-engine-host.test.ts driving the host with an injected `voice.RenderEngine` fake — the constructor already accepts one (voice-engine-host.ts:117-119) and `setMonitor` (:558) is the sink seam — whose `tick()` throws on the 5th call: (1) `host.start()` under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, advance 10 ticks, assert the host is still scheduled (`vi.getTimerCount() > 0`) and that ticks 6..10 happened; (2) assert the monitor sink received exactly ONE `error` event labelled 'Render frame faulted' on the first throw and a second only after the 120th consecutive throw (rate-limited so a 120 Hz fault cannot flood the Monitor bus and the #122 Reporter); (3) assert `step(dt)` called DIRECTLY still throws, so the catch lives in `loop()` only and existing tests that drive `step` keep their raw failure semantics. Implementation: wrap the `while (this.accumulator >= TICK_MS && steps < 12)` drain body (voice-engine-host.ts:471-477) in try/catch inside `loop()`, and additionally wrap the `this.loop()` call inside `scheduleNext`'s setTimeout so a throw in loop()'s own bookkeeping still reschedules; on catch bump `consecutiveFrameFaults`, emit the rate-limited monitor event, break the catch-up drain for that frame, set `this.accumulator = 0`, and reset the counter on the next clean frame.
design.reverses: `git revert` the single commit. Additive inside one class, no interface change, no persisted state — reverting restores the exact prior crash semantics. Nothing later depends on it; S3's fatal handler is independent.

design.title: fatal-shutdown.ts: darken without closing, then flush, then bounded-drain exit
design.intent: resilience-hole-0001's second half. main.ts:263 wires `onFatal: () => flushReportsSync()` — no blackout — so a hard crash leaves the Art-Net/sACN stream stopped mid-frame and the LEDs latched on. REPAIRED against the landed attack (raised independently by both reviewers) that a naive blackout never reaches the wire: packages/io/src/artnet.ts:74 and sacn.ts:115 use asynchronous `socket.send(...)`, and process-errors.ts:53-58 runs onFatal then `exit(1)` synchronously, so the darkening datagrams are discarded. So the fatal path (a) calls a NEW `darken()` on the host — clearTimeout + output.blackout, and explicitly NOT output.close(), because closing the socket before the datagrams flush is the same bug in a different place — (b) runs flushReportsSync, and (c) hands the exit to a bounded drain: process-errors.ts gains an optional `drainMs` (default 0, set to 100 by main.ts) so `exit(1)` is scheduled rather than called inline. A one-line wiring change inside a 0%-coverage module is unprovable, so the ordering and fault isolation live in a named, tested module.
design.verification: fatal-shutdown.test.ts: `createFatalHandler({ darken, flushReports, log })` — assert (1) call order is darken THEN flushReports (push to a shared array; the reverse ordering is what sonnet shipped and what the reviewers flagged, since process-errors wraps the whole callback in ONE try/catch so a throwing flush would abort before the rig darkens); (2) a `darken` that throws does not prevent `flushReports` and does not rethrow; (3) a `flushReports` that throws does not rethrow — each isolated in its own try/catch. process-errors.test.ts gains: with `drainMs: 100` and an injected `exit`, an uncaught exception calls onFatal synchronously but does NOT call exit(1) synchronously; under `vi.useFakeTimers()`, exit(1) fires exactly once after 100ms. voice-engine-host.test.ts + engine-host.test.ts gain: `darken()` calls `output.blackout(dmxMap)` and does NOT call `output.close()`, and clears the timer. main.ts change is exactly `onFatal: createFatalHandler({ darken: () => (voiceHost ?? host).darken(), flushReports: () => flushReportsSync() })` plus `drainMs: 100`. PARITY for the main.ts edit: `node scripts/server-smoke.mjs --engine voice|legacy` digests must equal the S0 baselines — the fatal path is never entered on a clean boot, so a changed digest means the wiring edit had a side effect and the step is wrong.
design.reverses: Revert to the literal `onFatal: () => flushReportsSync()`, drop `drainMs`, delete the two new files and the two `darken()` methods. NOTE the two deliberate orderings: rig before telemetry, and exit after drain. If a blackout is ever observed to hang the exit, lower drainMs or swap the order inside fatal-shutdown.ts rather than reverting the module; the 100ms window is the only period in which a process that has already thrown keeps running.

design.title: Extract createTrustedPostRoute; both HTTP routes on one owner, caps kept per-route
design.intent: duplicated-code-0006: host-event.ts:91-120 and native-midi.ts:48-77 are the same 28-line security preamble (path match, 405, isTrustedHost -> 401, setEncoding, byte-capped accumulation with req.destroy, error -> 400). One owner means a hardening change is applied once, and the drifted `MAX_BODY` named constant vs bare `4096` literal disappears as a NAME while both VALUES survive. SYNTHESIS DECISION on the question opus routed here and fable answered wrongly: the caps are NOT unified. fable's plan says both 'named per-route argument' and 'the drifted constants unify', and unification is mechanically falsified — host-event.ts:9 caps at 2048 and host-event.test.ts:205 sends exactly 'x'.repeat(4096); under a unified 4096 cap `4096 > 4096` is false and that test breaks, destroying the step's own zero-test-edit parity proof, while unifying downward to 2048 silently tightens the native-MIDI guard. Changing a guard VALUE is a separate decision and must not ride an extraction commit.
design.verification: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec vitest run src/http/` — host-event.test.ts and native-midi.test.ts pass UNMODIFIED (they are the parity oracle; if either needs an edit the extraction is not behaviour-preserving and the step is redone), with S1's new cases pinning native-midi's error branch and its 4096/4097 boundary through the move. New trusted-post.test.ts covers the shared surface directly: wrong path -> returns false (fall-through), non-POST -> 405, untrusted -> 401, over-cap -> destroy with the caller's message, request 'error' -> 400, happy path -> onBody(raw, res) invoked once with the accumulated string. Signature `createTrustedPostRoute({ path, hostToken, maxBody, tooLargeMessage, onBody })`; host-event passes `HOST_EVENT_MAX_BODY = 2048`, native-midi passes `NATIVE_MIDI_MAX_BODY = 4096` — grep the diff to confirm both values are present exactly once each and that no shared MAX_BODY constant was introduced.
design.reverses: `git revert`; both handlers return to their inlined preambles. Because the guard values were passed through rather than unified, the revert is a pure structural undo with no value drift to reconcile.

design.title: Client-side liveness watchdog in WSClient
design.intent: resilience-hole-0004, browser half: `link` is driven only by onopen/onclose (client.ts:198-218), so a half-open TCP link (wifi drop, laptop sleep, dead tunnel) leaves store.link === 'open' forever; hit() then sends into a socket that silently discards (client.ts:302) and the offline local sim is deliberately skipped because the server 'owns' resolution — the drummer hits pads and nothing lights. No new protocol is needed: the server already emits traffic continuously, so message-AGE is a sufficient signal, and it must be message-age rather than a ws-level pong because a browser answers pings invisibly at the transport layer. The window is 5000ms, not the 500ms sonnet chose (both reviewers landed on that: one GC pause, one route transition, one event-loop stall force-closes a healthy link mid-show).
design.verification: New/extended client.test.ts using the injected `WSFactory` fake (client.ts:37) and `vi.useFakeTimers()`: (1) open the socket, deliver NO messages, advance past the watchdog window -> assert `ws.close()` was called, `onConnection('closed')` fired, and a reconnect was armed (assert `reconnectAttempt` incremented); (2) deliver a message every window/2 -> no forced close after 10 windows; (3) after a 4401 auth close the watchdog is disarmed (no timer fires while the auth-error flag is set); (4) `close()` clears the watchdog (assert `vi.getTimerCount()` returns to 0); (5) BACKGROUND-TAB CASE — fire the interval callback once at t+20000 having delivered a message at t+19500 and assert NO close: staleness is computed from `now() - lastMessageAt`, never from tick count, so a browser clamping setInterval in a hidden tab can only delay detection, never manufacture a false positive. Implementation: record `lastMessageAt` at the TOP of `handleMessage` (client.ts:221, before decode, so a malformed frame still counts as liveness); arm the interval in `openSocket`, clear it in onclose/close; `WSClientOptions` gains `watchdogMs` (default 5000, chosen far above any plausible server cadence and NOT derived from the 10ms stats period, so a later cadence change cannot silently break it) and `now` (default Date.now) for tests.
design.reverses: `git revert`. The watchdog only ever forces a close the existing reconnect ladder already handles, so reverting restores exactly today's behaviour. If it proves too aggressive on a slow tunnel, raise `watchdogMs` rather than reverting.

design.title: Late-bind the monitor sink so process-error capture installs before the project load
design.intent: resilience-hole-0002's second aggravating factor: `installProcessErrorCapture` is wired at main.ts:263 but `initialProject()` runs at main.ts:155, so a boot crash is not captured, not reported, not even logged to the Monitor — the drummer just sees the process die. The capture cannot simply be hoisted: `monitor` -> `monitorBus` (main.ts:246) -> `broadcastJson` (main.ts:239) dereferences `const clients` (main.ts:232) at call time, so a hoisted handler that fires during boot throws a ReferenceError out of the handler itself and captures nothing — fable's variant hoisted without breaking this chain and the attack landed. Break it with a mutable sink rather than reordering the whole construction: a 3-line change that unblocks the hoist without moving any collaborator.
design.verification: PARITY: `node scripts/server-smoke.mjs --engine voice` and `--engine legacy` digests must equal the S0 baselines EXACTLY — including the monitor replay ORDER, which is what this step is most likely to perturb (the bus retains 300 events and replays on connect, so an event emitted before `clients` exists must still reach the first client in the same position). A digest diff in the monitor array means the step is wrong. INJECTED-FAULT PROBE (the check that proves the hoist did what it exists to do, and the replacement for fable's citation of a boot.test.ts that does not exist in this repo): temporarily add `throw new Error('boot-probe')` immediately after the hoisted `installProcessErrorCapture` call, run the smoke harness, confirm stdout carries '[process] uncaught exception: boot-probe' AND that the digest's monitor array contains the corresponding error event; remove the probe before committing and paste the captured stdout into the PR body. Implementation: `let broadcastSink: (msg: ServerMessage) => void = () => {};` then `const monitorBus = createMonitorBus((m) => broadcastSink(m));` above initialProject, `installProcessErrorCapture({ monitor, onFatal, drainMs })` immediately after, and `broadcastSink = broadcastJson;` at the current monitorBus construction site.
design.reverses: `git revert` restores the original construction order. Only main.ts changes and the sink indirection leaves no persisted trace.

design.title: Make the six ClientMessageDeps collaborators required — types only, zero runtime delta
design.intent: speculative-generality-0002, first half. Six collaborators are optional for a configuration that has never occurred (main.ts:618-663 is the only production wiring and supplies all six), and one of them, `backups`, guards a fail-CLOSED data-loss snapshot whose absent-branch default is `?? true`. Dropping that field from the object literal today compiles and silently disables the pre-risk snapshot. This commit drops the `?` and fixes the resulting test harnesses ONLY — every `?.` and `?? true` fallback stays, so the runtime is provably byte-identical and the commit is a pure compile-time tightening. The split from S9 exists because the finding itself flags the deletion half as removes_failure_path and it deserves its own revert boundary (a landed attack on fable, which bundled both in one commit).
design.verification: Re-confirm the single-wiring premise mechanically at execution time rather than trusting the Phase 2 read: `rg -n 'createClientMessageHandler|handleProjectMessage' apps/server/src --glob '!*.test.ts'` must return exactly the main.ts call site plus the definition and the internal call. Then drop `?` from tunnelControl, isTunnelClient, monitor, listNetworkAdapters, backups, controller on ClientMessageDeps and from ProjectHandlerDeps.snapshotPreRisk and run `pnpm typecheck` — every error must be a TEST harness; a single non-test error falsifies the premise and the step stops. Harnesses gain EXPLICIT no-op stubs (e.g. `backups: { list: () => [], restore: () => false, snapshotPreRisk: () => true }`) so 'backups disabled' becomes a stated test intent. Then `pnpm gates`. Because no runtime expression changes, `git diff -U0 -- apps/server/src/handlers/client-message.ts apps/server/src/handlers/projects.ts | grep '^[+-]'` must show only signature lines.
design.reverses: `git revert`. Purely a type change; reverting restores optionality and the explicit stubs become redundant but harmless.

design.title: Export createSnapshotReader from snapshot-store.ts
design.intent: The boot-recovery ladder (S10) needs to read the newest snapshot BEFORE `createSnapshotStore` can exist — the store requires `readCurrent`/`applyRestored` (main.ts:580-590), which at boot depend on the very engine that has not been constructed. Rather than duplicating the store's list/gunzip/parse path into the boot module, split its read half into `createSnapshotReader({ dir })` returning `{ list, read }` and have `createSnapshotStore` delegate. This is also the repair both reviewers prescribed for sonnet's alternative — forward-declaring `host`/`liveShowLibrary`/`liveSongLibrary` as `let`s so the store could be built early, which would make them possibly-undefined across hundreds of main.ts references that sonnet's file list and LOC estimate never accounted for.
design.verification: `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec vitest run src/backups/snapshot-store.test.ts` — the existing suite must pass UNMODIFIED; it is the oracle that delegation preserved listing order (newest-first by the numeric createdAt prefix), stem parsing (split on the FIRST dash so 'pre-risk' survives) and the corrupt-bundle -> null contract. Add two cases against the reader directly: `list()` on a dir containing a non-snapshot filename ignores it; `read()` on a truncated .gz returns null rather than throwing.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the store re-absorbs its read half. Must be reverted together with S10, which imports the reader.

design.title: Delete the now-unreachable absent-collaborator fallbacks
design.intent: speculative-generality-0002, second half — the half the finding flags as removes_failure_path, so it gets its own commit and its own revert boundary. With the fields required (S7), ~20 `deps.x?.` no-op branches (client-message.ts:215-306) and three data-loss-guard defaults are unreachable by type: `snapshotPreRisk: () => deps.backups?.snapshotPreRisk() ?? true` (client-message.ts:342), `if (deps.backups && !deps.backups.snapshotPreRisk())` (:441) and `if ((deps.snapshotPreRisk?.() ?? true) === false)` (projects.ts:40). Removing them turns a dropped `backups` field from a silent fail-open into a compile error.
design.verification: MUTATION PROBE, run BEFORE and AFTER: delete the `backups:` key from main.ts:645-652 in a scratch edit and run `pnpm typecheck` — before this step it compiles (that is the bug), after this step it must ERROR. Restore the key. Then a new test asserting the fail-closed DIRECTION survives the deletion: with `snapshotPreRisk: () => false`, a `loadProject` message must reply `{t:'error'}` and must NOT call `host.engine.setProject` (assert with a spy). Grep gate: `rg -n '\?\? true' apps/server/src/handlers/` returns zero hits. Then `pnpm gates`.
design.reverses: `git revert` restores the fallbacks. This is the one step in the plan that DELETES guard branches, so it is deliberately the smallest possible commit and depends on S7 having landed — reverting S9 alone restores the tolerant runtime while keeping the type tightening.

design.title: boot-project.ts: recovery ladder for an unloadable live project
design.intent: resilience-hole-0002: `initialProject()` runs at module scope (main.ts:155) and unconditionally calls `loadProject(LIVE_PROJECT)`, which throws on a ZodError or a ReferentialIntegrityError with no catch anywhere in the chain; the refuters sharpened the trigger (`setInputMap` is shape-checked but never integrity-checked, so a mapping naming a nonexistent drum can be autosaved and then brick the next boot), and the snapshot restore path needs a running WS server and a connected client, which by definition cannot exist. Extract the decision into a testable module with a real filesystem and give it a ladder: file -> newest snapshot -> seed. TWO REPAIRS forced by landed attacks. (a) ERROR-CLASS DISCRIMINATION: quarantine ONLY on SyntaxError / ZodError / ReferentialIntegrityError. loadProject (projects.ts:57-66) mixes readFileSync IO faults into the same catch site, so an EACCES/EMFILE/locked-file fault would otherwise permanently rename a perfectly good project aside and let the autosaver write a fresh seed over the name — a data-loss bug introduced by a data-loss fix. On an IO-class error: retry once, then fail loudly WITHOUT renaming. (b) WHOLE-BUNDLE RECOVERY: SnapshotBundle (snapshot-store.ts:41) carries project + showLibrary + songLibrary and applyRestoredSnapshot applies all three together, so recovering only the project would pair a rolled-back project with current on-disk libraries — a state combination the existing restore path never produces. The snapshot rung therefore returns the whole bundle, its project member goes through the SAME parseProject + assertProjectIntegrity pipeline as loadProject (reusing projects.ts, not duplicating it), a bundle whose project member fails continues down the ladder, and the boot wiring seeds liveShowLibrary/liveSongLibrary from the same bundle.
design.verification: New boot-project.test.ts against a real temp dir (the ladder is filesystem behaviour; faking it would prove nothing): (1) no file -> `source: 'seed'`, outputs reconciled to the canonical port count; (2) valid file -> `source: 'file'`, Project byte-identical to today's `loadProject` result; (3) truncated JSON + one valid snapshot in `<dir>/backups` -> `source: 'snapshot'`, bad file renamed to `default.local.corrupt-<ts>.json`, original filename absent, AND the returned bundle's showLibrary/songLibrary are the snapshot's, asserted to come from the same bundle id as the project; (4) schema-valid-but-dangling-drum-ref file (defaultProject() with an inputMap entry pointing at 'nope') + NO snapshot -> `source: 'recovered-seed'`, quarantined, `recovery.reason` names ReferentialIntegrityError; (5) corrupt SNAPSHOT plus corrupt file -> still `recovered-seed`, never a throw; (6) IO-FAULT CASE — an injected readFileSync that throws EACCES twice -> NO rename occurs, the original filename is still on disk, and the ladder reports the IO fault rather than silently seeding. `startupDiagnostics` widens `project.source` to `'seed' | 'file' | 'snapshot' | 'recovered-seed'`; `pnpm typecheck` catches every consumer and diagnostics.test.ts asserts the recovered-seed row is a `type: 'error'` Monitor event, not a quiet persistence row. END-TO-END: `node scripts/server-smoke.mjs --engine voice --seed-corrupt` (harness flag added here: writes a truncated default.local.json into the temp dir before boot) must produce a server that LISTENS — today it exits — with the recovery event in the digest's monitor array; the clean-boot digest must still equal the S0 baseline.
design.reverses: `git revert`; main.ts returns to the throwing `initialProject()`. IRREVERSIBLE RESIDUE: a file already quarantined to `default.local.corrupt-<ts>.json` stays renamed after a revert — the rollback runbook must include `mv projects/default.local.corrupt-*.json projects/default.local.json` (newest timestamp first). The error-class discrimination is what keeps that residue rare: only genuinely unparseable files are ever renamed.

design.title: Extract ws-broadcast.ts from main.ts — verbatim, no behaviour change
design.intent: divergent-change-0004, first drain. `broadcastJson`, `broadcastBinary`, `broadcastPresence` and `relayToOthers` (main.ts:239-244, 423-433, 429, 540-545) are the four socket-iterating closures over `clients`; they are also where resilience-hole-0005's backpressure guard must go, and they are 0%-covered. Move them into `createBroadcaster({ clients, encode })` with the bodies byte-identical and pin today's behaviour with tests. NO guard is added in this commit — that move-then-change split is what makes the guard's own revert safe, and it is the discipline sonnet's plan lacked (its S8 asserted an extraction it never planned, so its verification could not run).
design.verification: PURE-MOVE PROOF: `git show HEAD~1:apps/server/src/main.ts | sed -n '239,244p;423,433p;540,545p'` compared line by line against the corresponding bodies in ws-broadcast.ts — only the closure->parameter rebinding of `clients`/`encodeServer` may differ; a commit containing any logic edit is rejected and split. New ws-broadcast.test.ts with fake sockets pins today's contract: only `readyState === OPEN` sockets receive; the payload is encoded ONCE and the same string handed to every socket; `broadcastBinary` passes `{ binary: true }`; `relayToOthers` excludes the sender and only the sender; `broadcastPresence` sends a per-socket payload (assert two sockets get different `youAreEditor`). PARITY: smoke digests in both engine modes equal the S0 baselines.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the four closures return to main.ts. S14 lives in this module and must be reverted first.

design.title: Extract ws-connection.ts from main.ts — verbatim, no behaviour change
design.intent: divergent-change-0004, second drain, and the enabling move for resilience-hole-0013 and the server half of resilience-hole-0004. The entire `wss.on('connection')` body (main.ts:470-533) — admit decision, tunnelClients tagging, presence, initial state, monitor replay, the message try/catch, close/error cleanup — is 0%-covered and is where three findings must be fixed. Move it behind `createWsConnectionHandler(deps)` with bodies byte-identical.
design.verification: PURE-MOVE PROOF: `git show HEAD~1:apps/server/src/main.ts | sed -n '470,533p'` diffed against the new handler body — only closure->deps rebinding may differ. New ws-connection.test.ts with fake sockets and fake `IncomingMessage`s pins today's contract exactly: a wrong PIN closes with the decision's code/reason and never admits; a cf-forwarded connection is tagged as a tunnel client (main.ts:494); ORDER is presence-then-state-then-replay asserted with a single ordered log array (the comment at main.ts:492-500 says this ordering is load-bearing and nothing currently proves it — it is also one of S0's negative-control mutations); a binary frame is ignored; a decode failure emits a 'WebSocket decode error' monitor event AND an error frame while keeping the socket open; a handler throw emits 'WebSocket handler error'; close and error both call `clients.remove`, `controllerMonitor.dropWatcher` and `broadcastPresence`. PARITY: smoke digests in both engine modes equal the S0 baselines — this is the largest single move in the plan and the digest is the only end-to-end check on it.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the connection body returns inline to main.ts. S13/S15/S16 all live in or wire through this module and must be reverted first.

design.title: ws-keepalive.ts: ping/pong reaper for dead peers
design.intent: resilience-hole-0004, server half: the connection handler installs only `close` and `error` listeners (main.ts:520-531), so a dead peer is never reaped and stays in the broadcast registry — which is also what lets resilience-hole-0005's buffer grow forever. Use the standard `ws` keepalive (interval pings, terminate any peer that did not pong since the previous sweep) rather than a protocol-level message, so packages/protocol is untouched and browsers answer automatically at the transport layer. The sweeper gets its OWN module generic over a `{ ping(); terminate(); on('pong', cb) }` shape rather than living in client-registry.ts, whose documented contract is `CloseableSocket { close() }` and which is deliberately ws-decoupled 'so it is trivially unit-testable' (client-registry.ts:1-6) — fable put it there and the attack landed as an undeclared interface widening. The same sweep clock is what S14's slow-peer strikes are counted on.
design.verification: New cases with fake sockets and `vi.useFakeTimers()`: (1) a socket that never emits 'pong' is `terminate()`d on the second sweep and removed via the injected `onDead` (which main.ts wires to the exact body of today's close handler: `clients.remove` + `controllerMonitor.dropWatcher` + `broadcastPresence`, so a reaped peer is indistinguishable from a normal disconnect to every other subsystem); (2) a socket that pongs after each ping survives 10 sweeps; (3) a socket admitted mid-sweep is NOT terminated on the immediately following sweep (alive flag initialised true at admit — the classic off-by-one that reaps healthy newcomers); (4) the interval is `unref()`d so it never keeps the process alive, and boot.ts's shutdown calls the returned disposer (assert it). Sweep period is the named constant `HEARTBEAT_MS = 15_000`, asserted by the tests so a value change is a visible test change. MANDATORY LIVE CHECK before merge, recorded in the PR body, since no unit test covers a real half-open socket: `pnpm dev`, connect a phone over the LAN, airplane-mode it mid-session, confirm from the server Monitor that the peer is reaped within two sweeps and the headcount drops; and confirm over a 5-minute idle session that NO healthy peer is reaped.
design.reverses: `git revert`; no keepalive, peers linger exactly as today. This is the step most able to disconnect a healthy client (a browser that stops answering pings under heavy main-thread load), so if a false reap is observed, raise HEARTBEAT_MS or require three missed sweeps before reverting the module. S14 counts its strikes on this sweep and must be reverted first.

design.title: Backpressure skip on the high-rate streams + slow-peer termination on the keepalive clock
design.intent: resilience-hole-0005: `broadcastJson` gates only on readyState, so a peer that cannot drain 100 messages/second (a phone over the Cloudflare tunnel, a collapsed TCP window) accumulates undeliverable frames inside the Node process for as long as the socket stays technically OPEN — which, per resilience-hole-0004, is forever on a half-open link. Now that the broadcaster is a tested module the guard is provable. TWO REPAIRS forced by landed attacks. (a) STRIKE CLOCK DECOUPLED: strikes are counted on S13's 15s keepalive sweep, NEVER per broadcast — fable counted 3 strikes on a 100 Hz broadcast, which terminates a peer after ~30ms of wall clock, and even opus's 30 sweeps is ~300ms; on the sweep clock, termination needs 3 x 15s = 45s of sustained over-threshold, an order of magnitude longer than the client's own 5s self-recovery. (b) SKIP CONFINED TO THE HIGH-RATE STREAMS: the skip applies to the 100 Hz stats broadcast and the ~30fps binary preview only; event-driven messages (state, presence, monitor, error) always send. Both reviewers landed the attack that skipping ALL traffic starves the very message-age signal S5's watchdog measures, so a slow-but-alive peer would be declared dead by its own client while the server struck it out. This confines the starvation window and moves termination far beyond it; the residual — whether a tiny keepalive frame should be added to the wire protocol so a skipped-but-alive peer keeps its watchdog fed at all — is costed and routed to Trent rather than silently absorbed, because it is the one repair here that would change packages/protocol.
design.verification: New cases with a fake socket exposing a settable `bufferedAmount`: (1) a socket reporting 2_000_000 is skipped on the stats/preview paths while its OPEN sibling still receives, and the skip is counted on the returned `stats()`; (2) the SAME over-threshold socket still receives `state`, `presence`, `monitor` and `error` messages — this is the test that pins repair (b) and it must fail if the skip is applied indiscriminately; (3) a socket that drops back under the threshold resumes receiving and its consecutive-over counter resets to 0; (4) strikes advance ONLY when the keepalive sweep fires — assert that 10_000 simulated broadcasts at the same over-threshold state advance the counter by ZERO, and that three sweeps advance it to three; (5) at the third sweep the socket has `terminate()` called exactly once, is removed via S13's `onDead`, and receives no further sends; (6) an injected monitor sink got exactly one `error` event naming the dropped peer. Threshold and sweep count are named constants in the module (`BACKPRESSURE_BYTES = 1_000_000`, `SLOW_PEER_SWEEPS = 3` on the 15s clock) asserted by the tests. MANDATORY LIVE CHECK before merge, recorded in the PR body, since the failure this step can actually cause — disconnecting a legitimate client — is exactly what a fake socket cannot reproduce: `pnpm dev`, two normal browser tabs plus one throttled to 'Slow 3G' in devtools, drive input for 60s, confirm from the Monitor panel that no healthy peer was dropped and that the throttled tab either keeps rendering or recovers by reconnect rather than looping.
design.reverses: `git revert` the commit; ws-broadcast.ts returns to the readyState-only gate from S11. Because S11 is a separate commit, this revert restores exactly today's broadcast semantics without undoing the extraction or its tests. If only the termination is too aggressive, raise SLOW_PEER_SWEEPS or drop the terminate branch while keeping the skip — the skip alone is the memory-safety half.

design.title: Error-frame redaction as a pure function + per-socket rate limit
design.intent: resilience-hole-0013: the message catch (main.ts:509-517) sends `err.message` verbatim to the client — for a ZodError a schema path dump, for a filesystem fault an absolute path on the drummer's machine, handed to whoever holds the room PIN over a public Cloudflare tunnel. It is also the only unrate-limited error surface, and each frame emits a Monitor event feeding the #122 Reporter. The server already knows which sockets are remote (`tunnelClients`, main.ts:494), so the redaction branch has what it needs. GRAFT from fable: the redaction is a PURE `clientErrorMessage(err: unknown, viaTunnel: boolean, ref: string): string` in the existing tested ws-protocol.ts rather than logic embedded in a connection handler — it is the piece that can be exhaustively table-tested, and the fable-refuter's own attack on sonnet's version was that the redaction had no declared test home. The per-socket limiter needs socket state and stays in ws-connection.ts.
design.verification: ws-protocol.test.ts truth table for `clientErrorMessage`: a multi-line ZodError-shaped message and an absolute-path Error, viaTunnel true -> output matches /^Could not apply that change \(ref [0-9a-f]{8}\)$/ and `expect(out).not.toContain('/')`; viaTunnel false -> first line only, capped at 300 chars, still carrying the ref. ws-connection.test.ts: (1) a handler throw carrying `/Users/someone/projects/default.local.json` on a tunnel-tagged socket produces the redacted frame; (2) the SAME correlation ref appears in the Monitor event, whose `detail` still carries the full message and stack — the diagnostic must not be degraded, only the outbound frame; (3) 50 malformed messages in one second yield at most 5 error frames while all 50 still emit Monitor events, and frames 6..50 are silently dropped; (4) after the rate window elapses, error frames resume. Local sockets keep the fuller message but route through the same limiter.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the catch returns to sending `err.message` verbatim with no limit, and clientErrorMessage is deleted from ws-protocol.ts. Isolated to one catch block plus one pure function.

design.title: Connection cap in the WS connection path
design.intent: resilience-hole-0005's amplifier: `clients.admit(ws)` is additive with no maximum (main.ts:493, comment 'Admit additively (no eviction)'), so a shared room link multiplies the per-client stats stream without limit on the machine driving a live show. Sequenced after the connection handler is extracted and testable. REPAIRED against the landed attack on opus's absolutist stance (a plain constant with no env override means a venue that exceeds the cap can only be fixed by cutting an OTA release): the constant is the DEFAULT and a single `LEDRUMS_MAX_CLIENTS` read once at boot overrides it. A one-shot env read of an operational limit is configuration, not the speculative generality this initiative deletes elsewhere — the repo already reads LEDRUMS_* for engine, ports and projects dir.
design.verification: New cases: with `MAX_CLIENTS_DEFAULT = 32`, the 33rd connection is closed with a distinct close code (4429) and reason, is never passed to `clients.admit`, never receives `state`, and never triggers `broadcastPresence`; the 33rd succeeds again after one of the 32 closes. ORDERING (the classic admission-guard bug): assert the cap is checked AFTER the PIN/host-token admit decision — 32 admitted clients plus one WRONG-PIN dial must still return close code 4401, not 4429, so an unauthorised dial can never consume a slot. ENV: `LEDRUMS_MAX_CLIENTS=4` yields a cap of 4; an unset, empty, zero, negative or non-numeric value falls back to 32 (assert each, so a typo cannot lock everyone out).
design.reverses: `git revert`; admission returns to unbounded. Isolated to one branch in one function; the env var stops being read and is harmless if left set.

design.title: Extract stats-frame.ts — pure stats adaptation + named cadence constant
design.intent: divergent-change-0004, third drain. main.ts:748-772 adapts the voice engine's stats onto the legacy `stats` shape (including a bar computed from beatsPerBar off the OTHER host) inside a setInterval callback — real policy, zero coverage, and the site of the cadence decision. Extract `buildStatsMessage({ voiceHost, host, beatsPerBar })` as a pure function and name the cadence `STATS_INTERVAL_MS = 10`. The VALUE is unchanged: all three variants agreed the 100 Hz cadence is visible to the drummer (latency readout, fps number, per-voice meters) and is therefore a taste call, not a correctness one — it goes to Trent as an open question with the constant named and ready.
design.verification: New stats-frame.test.ts with stub hosts: voice mode maps timeMs/beat/voiceCount -> activeTriggers/pixelCount and computes `bar = Math.floor(beat / beatsPerBar)` — assert the exact floor behaviour at beat 7.9 with beatsPerBar 4 (bar 1) and assert `tickCount` is still the literal 0 the current code emits; legacy mode returns `{t:'stats', stats: s.engine, …}` with NO `voice` key (assert `'voice' in msg === false`, since an added key changes the wire payload). PARITY: the smoke digest's first three stats frames — after normalisation strips latencyMs/fps/timeMs/beat — must equal the S0 baselines in BOTH engine modes; that is what proves the adaptation moved without drift.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the adaptation returns inline. Pure move plus a constant, no behaviour surface.

design.title: Collapse the show/song persisted-slot duplication into createPersistedSlot
design.intent: divergent-change-0004's actual day-to-day pain: adding a persisted slot today means five separate edits to main.ts (loader, live `let`, autosaver with its three near-identical monitor hooks, stateMessage field, shutdown flush). liveShowLibrary/liveSongLibrary (main.ts:178-205) are the same five lines twice and the createAutosaver calls differ only in a destination string. `createPersistedSlot({ label, destination, load, inspect, save, monitor })` returns `{ get, set, autosaver, loadInfo }` so a new slot is one registration. Scoped to the TWO BLOB SLOTS ONLY: the project slot is explicitly excluded because its live value is engine state — the autosaver reads through `host.engine.getProject()` (main.ts:167) and the voice host mutates that object in place, so a slot-owned get/set would create a dual source of truth or a lying accessor. Sonnet's variant built the primitive around three slots and the attack landed; this plan carries a one-line comment at the project autosaver saying why it is not a slot. Deliberately LAST, and deliberately NOT divergent-change-0004's full `createServerApp` + registry rewrite — a 600-LOC re-wiring of an untested module is exactly the change whose defect is found by a drummer rather than a test.
design.verification: New persisted-slot.test.ts: `set()` marks the autosaver dirty exactly once per call; a null slot's save sink is a no-op (today's `liveShowLibrary ? saveShowLibraryAsync(...) : Promise.resolve()` behaviour, main.ts:190-205) and does NOT emit an onSaved monitor event; the three monitor hooks emit `persistence`/`persistence`/`error` carrying the slot's destination string — assert the exact label strings ('Show library autosave scheduled'/'saved'/'failed') so the wire-visible Monitor rows are pinned. Then `pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec vitest run src/show-library.test.ts src/song-library.test.ts src/autosave.test.ts` unmodified and green. PARITY: smoke digests equal the S0 baselines with special attention to the monitor array — these autosavers emit named rows the digest captures, so a renamed label shows up as a digest diff.
design.reverses: `git revert`; the two library slots return to their duplicated form. Because the Monitor label strings are pinned by tests and by the digest, a revert cannot silently change what the drummer sees in the Monitor panel.

interface_deltas.note: No exported symbol changes. The reduction is in the deps CONTRACT: six optional collaborators become required and ~20 absent-collaborator branches plus three `?? true` data-loss-guard defaults are deleted, so the number of configurations the module claims to support drops from 2^7 to the one that actually ships. Fewer states per unit of behaviour is the reduction claimed.

Deliberate, and it passes the two-real-callers test on day one. Two independent implementations of the same 28-line security preamble become one owner plus two configurations; the duplicated BEHAVIOUR surface halves while the export count rises by two. The alternative — leaving it duplicated — has already drifted once (named MAX_BODY vs the 4096 literal). The two cap VALUES are parameters, not unified.

interface_deltas.at: apps/server/src (composition root: main.ts drained into ws-broadcast / ws-connection / ws-keepalive / stats-frame / boot-project / fatal-shutdown / persisted-slot)
interface_deltas.note: Unavoidable and stated honestly: main.ts is a side-effecting entry module that exports NOTHING, so any decomposition can only add exported symbols — there is no symbol count to reduce. The objective is change-locality and testability, measured by two numbers rather than interface size: main.ts drops from 801 lines to roughly 350, and the extracted logic goes from 0% covered to covered by seven new suites. No interface win is claimed; the finding's real cost — every feature edits the root — is paid down.

+2 exports to avoid duplicating the list/gunzip/parse path into the boot-recovery module, and to avoid the alternative that both reviewers rejected (forward-declaring host/liveShowLibrary/liveSongLibrary so the whole store could be constructed early). The SnapshotStore interface is unchanged and now delegates to the reader — one implementation, two entry points.

One method per host: clearTimeout + output.blackout WITHOUT output.close(). Needed because stop() closes the transport, which on the fatal path discards the very datagrams the blackout exists to send. Both are on the live output path, hence S3's high risk rating.

One optional field, default 0 (today's behaviour exactly). Set to 100 by main.ts so exit(1) is scheduled rather than called inline, giving the async dgram blackout a bounded window to leave the socket. The cost is stated in S3's reverses: a process that has already thrown keeps running for 100ms.
Pure redaction function placed in the existing tested protocol module rather than inline-untestable in a connection handler — the graft taken from fable's variant.

No new exports; WSClientOptions gains two optional fields (`watchdogMs`, `now`). `now` exists solely so the watchdog is testable with fake timers — knowingly the one place in this plan where a field exists for tests rather than for production.

Explicitly untouched. The keepalive sweeper does NOT go here: CloseableSocket is documented as close()-only 'so it is trivially unit-testable' (client-registry.ts:1-6), and planting ping/pong/terminate there would be an undeclared widening of a deliberately ws-decoupled contract.

checks: `pnpm gates` (machine-mutex, typecheck + full suite) green on committed HEAD after EVERY step — 2968 tests at baseline, monotonically rising as each step adds its own suite; a step that leaves the count flat added no evidence and has not met its own bar.

S0 harness proving gate, run before any step may cite it: two identical runs byte-identical in BOTH engine modes, an explicit retained-key allow-list and redaction list written into artifacts/smoke-normalisation.md, and TWO negative-control mutations (drop one monitor emit; swap presence-then-state ordering) that must EACH produce a digest diff.

`node scripts/server-smoke.mjs --engine voice --out /tmp/step.json && diff /tmp/step.json docs/plans/2026-07-26-deep-review/artifacts/smoke-baseline-voice.json` — required on every step whose files include apps/server/src/main.ts (S3, S6, S10, S11, S12, S17, S18). An empty diff is the parity proof for the 0%-coverage entry module.

The same smoke diff against smoke-baseline-legacy.json with `--engine legacy`. Both modes run because main.ts:72 still defaults to LEGACY when LEDRUMS_ENGINE is unset while every shipping path forces voice (scripts/dev.mjs:32, src-tauri/lib.rs:386) — a change proven only in voice mode would silently break `pnpm start`.

Pure-move proof for each verbatim extraction (S11, S12, S17): `git show HEAD~1:apps/server/src/main.ts | sed -n '<range>p'` diffed against the new module body, reviewed line by line; only closure->parameter rebinding may differ. An extraction commit containing any logic edit is rejected and split.

`pnpm --filter @ledrums/server exec vitest run src/http/` with host-event.test.ts and native-midi.test.ts UNMODIFIED across S4 — the pre-existing route tests are the oracle for the trusted-POST extraction; needing to edit them falsifies it. Plus S1's boundary case, which is the only test that fails if a cap VALUE moves (the pre-existing 5000-byte case does not).

Mutation probe for S9: scratch-delete the `backups:` key from main.ts:645-652, `pnpm typecheck`, confirm it compiles BEFORE the step and ERRORS after, then restore. The only check that proves the fail-open hole is closed rather than relocated.

`rg -n 'createClientMessageHandler|handleProjectMessage' apps/server/src --glob '!*.test.ts'` before S7 — the single-production-wiring premise the whole speculative-generality fix rests on, re-confirmed at execution time rather than trusted from the Phase 2 read.

Injected-fault probe for S6: a temporary `throw` immediately after the hoisted `installProcessErrorCapture`, run under the smoke harness, must produce '[process] uncaught exception: boot-probe' on stdout AND the matching monitor row in the digest; probe removed before commit, captured stdout pasted into the PR.

Drain proof for S3: with `drainMs: 100` and an injected `exit`, assert exit(1) is NOT called synchronously and fires exactly once after the fake-timer advance — the check that separates 'blackout was invoked' from 'blackout had time to leave the socket'.

Starvation proof for S14: an over-threshold socket still receives state/presence/monitor/error frames, and 10_000 simulated broadcasts advance the strike counter by ZERO while three keepalive sweeps advance it to three.

Manual live checks recorded in the PR body, for the two steps that can disconnect a healthy client: S13 (a LAN phone airplane-moded mid-session, reaped within two sweeps; plus a 5-minute idle session with no healthy reap) and S14 (three tabs, one throttled to Slow 3G, 60s of input, no healthy peer dropped).
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps: Five regions where a green `pnpm gates` proves nothing, and what stands in for it. (1) apps/server/src/main.ts is imported by no test — a side-effecting entry module excluded from the server package's 72.31% line coverage. Substitute: the S0 smoke digest, a real boot of the real process in both engine modes, now with a written normalisation allow-list and a negative control so the oracle itself is proven rather than assumed. Its remaining weakness is that it observes STARTUP only, so a fault needing a connected editor and a mutation is outside it. (2) The uncaughtException path (S2/S3) cannot be exercised by vitest without killing the runner, so process-errors.ts injects proc/exit and the tests prove the handler contract, not that Node routes a render-loop throw into it; the S6 probe proves the wiring for a BOOT-time throw and a render-loop throw reaching the same handler is inferred, not observed — flagged as an inference. (3) Whether the blackout datagram physically leaves the NIC before exit is NOT proven: the drain test proves exit is withheld for 100ms and the fake output proves blackout-not-close, but packages/io's `socket.send(pkt, port, host, () => {})` is asynchronous and no test in this repo touches a real Art-Net/sACN socket. Confirming the rig actually darkens on a crash needs the bench kit, and is the single most important manual check before this initiative is called done. (4) No test touches a real half-open TCP connection — S13's reaper and S14's backpressure are proven against fake sockets with a settable bufferedAmount and a controllable pong. The failure they can cause (dropping a client that was actually fine) is exactly the one a fake socket cannot reproduce, hence the two mandatory live checks. The residual starvation interaction between S14's skip and S5's message-age watchdog is MITIGATED (skip confined to the high-rate streams; strikes on the 15s clock) but not eliminated — a peer whose link cannot drain 100 Hz will still self-close and reconnect, and whether that is acceptable or wants a protocol-level keepalive frame is an open question for Trent, not a solved problem. (5) Timing: S2's per-frame catch is tested under fake timers, which proves control flow, not the real-time budget; the try/catch is zero-cost on the happy path in V8 but that is a claim from the language, not a measurement — the smoke harness's stats frames carry `fps` if a measurement is wanted. Explicitly NOT claimed: parity for LEDRUMS_ENGINE=legacy beyond what the smoke digest observes, since the legacy path has no dedicated suite either. Also stated honestly: S2, S3, S10 and S15 deliberately CHANGE behaviour on fault paths (crash -> skip frame, crash -> darken-then-exit, crash -> recovered boot, verbatim error -> redacted). Parity is claimed only for non-fault paths; each fault path carries its own named positive test instead of a parity claim.
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.baseline_reference: Phase 0 baseline sha 3708648 (feat/ota-discord-announce), 2968 tests green at HEAD, apps/server line coverage 72.31% / branches 83.12% (00-coverage.json). Smoke digests are captured at the HEAD S0 lands on — AFTER fix batches 1-3 (dead-code auto-fixes, dead-code residue, kit-mirror removal) — not at 3708648; both digest files record the sha they were taken at so a stale baseline is detectable.

rollback_strategy: Nineteen commits, nineteen revert boundaries, and no commit depends on a later one — that is the point of the shape. Ordered pairs that must be reverted in the stated order: S8 before S10 in landing order and S10 before S8 in revert order (the boot ladder imports the snapshot reader); S7 before S9 landing, S9 before S7 reverting (the fallback deletion assumes required types); S11 before S14, S12 before S13/S15/S16, and S13 before S14 (the guards live inside or count on the extracted modules). Reverting a guard step alone is always safe and always restores today's behaviour, because every extraction is a separate commit from the change it enables — that separation is the plan's main rollback asset, and it is what sonnet's single 800-line relocation gave away. No feature flags and no runtime kill switches: a flag on a render-loop catch or a broadcast guard would itself be a new untested branch in the hot path, the wrong trade for code this small. Exactly ONE irreversible residue: S10 renames an unloadable project to `default.local.corrupt-<ts>.json` and reverting the code leaves it renamed — runbook step `mv projects/default.local.corrupt-*.json projects/default.local.json` (newest timestamp first), called out in S10's own `reverses`; the error-class discrimination added there is what keeps that residue rare rather than triggerable by a transient EACCES. No schema migration, no wire-protocol change and no persisted-format change occurs anywhere in this plan, so a full revert leaves disk state loadable by the reverted code. Panic path: `git revert --no-commit <S18>..<S0-parent>`, then `pnpm gates`, then confirm the smoke digests return to the S0 baselines — that is how the revert is confirmed complete rather than assumed.

open_questions.question: INIT-01-single-render-stack and INIT-04 rewrite the same file and MUST NOT run concurrently under any schedule pressure. INIT-01's plan asserts it should land first, on the grounds that decomposing main.ts around a two-engine branch bakes that branch into the new modules; this plan is built to be independent (every extraction moves the `voiceHost ?? host` branch verbatim into its new home, where INIT-01's deletion becomes a smaller, better-tested edit than deleting it from an 801-line untested file). Recommendation: INIT-04 first, because S2/S3/S10 are the steps that stop a live show from dying, they are cheap, and S0's smoke harness would materially de-risk INIT-01's 15-step strangler. Which lands first is Trent's call.

Should the 100 Hz stats broadcast cadence (main.ts:772, `}, 10);`) be lowered? A UI cannot render 100 updates/second and the preview stream is already throttled to ~30 fps, so this is roughly 10x the useful rate on every connected socket including remote phones — and it is the load behind resilience-hole-0005. But it is directly visible to the drummer (latency readout, fps number, per-voice meters) so it is a taste call, not a correctness one. All three variants refused to change it unilaterally. This plan does not change it: S17 names the constant `STATS_INTERVAL_MS = 10` and leaves the value, so the change is a one-line follow-up once the meters have been looked at at 20 Hz and 30 Hz.

Should a render-loop fault escalate beyond surviving the frame? S2 contains the throw and keeps ticking, so a permanently-broken authored effect produces a rate-limited error stream and a rig that renders everything except that effect — frozen-lit but recoverable, with the app and UI alive so the offending effect can be deleted mid-show. The rejected alternative is sonnet's auto-stop (blackout AND close the transport after N faults), which both reviewers killed: nothing restarts a stopped host, so the whole kit goes dark until relaunch, and at 120fps the threshold trips in ~42ms. Options: (a) ship S2 as written; (b) add a persistent UI banner naming the faulting frame; (c) push effect identity out of packages/core through the existing onDiagnostic seam so the HOST can quarantine one effect while core stays pure. Recommendation (c) as a follow-up initiative — it is an architecture-shaping call about what core is allowed to know.

Should a backpressure-skipped-but-alive peer be kept fed with a tiny protocol-level keepalive frame? Both reviewers landed the attack that skipping the high-rate streams starves the message-age signal S5's client watchdog measures. S14 mitigates it two ways (the skip is confined to stats/preview so event-driven messages still flow; strikes are counted on the 15s keepalive sweep so termination needs ~45s versus the client's 5s self-recovery) but does not eliminate it: a peer that genuinely cannot drain will self-close and reconnect. The full repair the reviewers asked for is a new `{t:'ping'}` ServerMessage (packages/protocol/src/schemas.ts:387-427) sent to skipped sockets — about six lines, but it is the only change in this plan that would touch the wire protocol, and the plan's 'no protocol change' rollback claim rests on not making it. Accept client-driven reconnect as the recovery, or add the frame?

When S10's boot recovery quarantines an unloadable project and falls back to a snapshot bundle or the seed, is a Monitor `error` row sufficient, or must the app show a blocking 'we recovered your project from a backup — your last edits may be missing' banner requiring acknowledgement? The silent-recovery failure mode is worse than the crash it replaces: a drummer who does not notice can author on top of a week-old snapshot. The plan implements the Monitor row and returns the outcome in the widened `source` field so a banner is a small web-side follow-up, but whether recovery is allowed to be quiet is a product call.

What is the real connection-cap ceiling? S16 ships `MAX_CLIENTS_DEFAULT = 32` with a `LEDRUMS_MAX_CLIENTS` override, but 32 is a guess — the largest rehearsal/venue scenario is unknown here, and a cap that locks out a legitimate viewer during a show is worse than no cap. If the real ceiling is known the constant should be that number; if it genuinely varies by venue, it may deserve to be a project setting rather than an env var.

Does `scripts/server-smoke.mjs` belong to this initiative or to the review programme as a whole? It is the only mechanism in any plan that produces parity evidence for a 0%-coverage entry module, and INIT-01, INIT-03 and INIT-11 all touch server boot paths that would benefit. This plan lands it as S0 — its own commit, touching nothing in apps/ or packages/ — so it is already shareable as-is; the question is only whether it should be sequenced ahead of ALL initiatives, which would make its normaliser and digest schema a cross-initiative contract rather than this initiative's private instrument.

synthesis_inputs.rationale: SKELETON: opus, the only variant both reviewers scored sound-with-repairs and the only one whose evidence model survives the initiative's governing fact — main.ts is imported by zero tests, so `pnpm gates` cannot fail for a wiring bug in the file where four of the eight findings live. Its instrument-first, move-then-change discipline (verbatim extraction in one commit, the behaviour change in a separate later commit against the now-testable module) is what gives every guard its own safe revert. DROPPED — sonnet entirely: its S2 relocated ~800 lines of 0%-coverage wiring in a single commit whose parity evidence cannot fail (fable rated it FATAL, opus major), five further steps were broken (S4's auto-stop-to-dead-rig, S5's forward-referenced snapshotStore that makes host possibly-undefined across main.ts, S7's 500ms watchdog, S9's test with no declared file, S10's wave-1 verification citing a file S2 creates later), and its S1 built a generic primitive around three slots when only two fit it. DROPPED — fable's centre of gravity: it verifies four main.ts-wiring steps with grep, gates and a citation of a boot.test.ts that does not exist in this repo; its S4 hoisted installProcessErrorCapture without breaking the monitor->broadcastJson->clients TDZ chain; its S8 counted slow-peer strikes on the 100 Hz broadcast clock (~30ms to terminate); and its S2 both kept and unified the body caps, which host-event.test.ts:205 mechanically falsifies. GRAFTED FROM FABLE onto the opus skeleton: clientErrorMessage as a PURE function in the already-tested ws-protocol.ts rather than logic buried in a connection handler (S15); the refusal of speculative machinery in the render-loop catch (no per-effect quarantine, no auto-stop); and fable's explicit routing of the render-fault posture and the stats cadence to Trent, which opus also did and sonnet did not. GRAFTED FROM SONNET: the keepalive as its own module rather than inside client-registry.ts (S13, also the opus-refuter's prescribed repair for fable), and the LEDRUMS_MAX_CLIENTS env override (S16), which repairs opus's absolutist no-knob stance. EVERY LANDED ATTACK ANSWERED: S0 gains a written normalisation allow-list plus two negative-control mutations that must diff (opus-refuter, unproven oracle); S1's false 'no cap test' premise is replaced by the genuinely unpinned req.on('error') branch plus a 4096/4097 boundary case (opus-refuter, native-midi.test.ts:145 exists); S3 darkens WITHOUT closing the transport and bounds exit(1) on a 100ms drain via a new process-errors drainMs (both refuters: dgram send is async, exit is synchronous), with a new host `darken()` because stop() closes; S4 keeps the two caps per-route and the synthesis settles opus's open question against fable's unification (both refuters, mechanically falsified); S10 discriminates IO faults from corruption before renaming a drummer's project aside AND recovers project+libraries from the same bundle through the existing parseProject/assertProjectIntegrity pipeline (opus-refuter x2, fable-refuter on the bundle mapping); S13 moves the keepalive out of client-registry.ts (opus-refuter on fable); S14 confines the skip to the high-rate streams and moves the strike clock onto the 15s sweep (both refuters on the starvation interaction; fable-refuter on the 100 Hz strike clock), with the residual protocol-keepalive question costed and routed to Trent; S16 gains an env override (opus-refuter); and the ['S16','S18'] boot.ts wave collision is serialised into separate waves (both refuters). Attacks the plan DEFENDED rather than repaired are carried forward with their defences intact: the digest's achievable stability (bounded capture + hard pre-trust gate), the RenderEngine injection seam (verified at voice-engine-host.ts:117-119), the frozen-lit posture (routed to Trent, not chosen silently), and the plan's size versus P1 urgency (S2 lands in wave 2, S10 in wave 5, ahead of every decomposition step).
